title: Kon-Tiki: Across the Pacific by Raft
author: Thor Heyerdahl
edition_analyzed: Standard English-language edition, originally translated in 1950
target_audience: Readers interested in true adventure stories
Fans of exploration and travel literature
Individuals curious about Polynesian history and anthropology
Students of cultural studies and marine navigation
General audiences interested in extraordinary human achievement
core_themes: Human curiosity and the spirit of adventure
Testing scientific hypotheses through practical experiment
The endurance and adaptability of humans in nature
The power of teamwork and camaraderie
primary_purpose: To chronicle and provide a first-hand account of the Kon-Tiki raft expedition in 1947, undertaken to demonstrate that ancient peoples could have made long sea voyages, connecting South America and Polynesia, and potentially contributed to the peopling of the Pacific islands.

structure_format.narrative_style: First-person, vivid, reflective, blending scientific observation with storytelling
structure_format.organization: Chronological, from conception/planning, through construction, voyage, and conclusion; interspersed with background on anthropology and personal anecdotes
features: Descriptions of daily life and group dynamics aboard the raft
Scientific background and discussions of relevant theories
Firsthand encounters with marine wildlife and the open ocean

key_concepts_lessons: Scientific ideas can be investigated through daring and unconventional methods.
Ancient people may have been capable of sea journeys long dismissed as impossible.
Adaptability, optimism, and teamwork are crucial in challenging, high-risk environments.
Real-world experience can challenge or enrich theoretical knowledge.
Respect and wonder for the natural world are heightened through close encounters.
style_tone: At times tense, emphasizing risk and uncertainty
notable_features: One of the best-known true adventure books of the 20th century
Results in significant public and scholarly debate about Pacific migration
Popularized Heyerdahl and spurred greater interest in experimental archaeology
Inspired a successful documentary film (which won an Academy Award)
Richly illustrated, often includes photographs from the expedition
cultural_historical_context: Published shortly after World War II, 'Kon-Tiki' tapped into renewed global interest in exploration, possibility, and rewriting human history. The expedition and Heyerdahl’s theory challenged mainstream scholarly ideas about Polynesian settlement, and, through wide publicity, influenced later discussions of migration and human ingenuity.
reception_impact: International bestseller, translated into dozens of languages
Generated massive public interest in adventure and anthropology
Sparked debate among academics over the possibility of South American influence in Polynesia
Established Thor Heyerdahl as a world-famous explorer and author
Enduring classic, frequently recommended for young readers and explorers
comparable_titles: Endurance: Shackleton’s Incredible Voyage by Alfred Lansing
The Lost City of Z by David Grann
The Voyage of the Beagle by Charles Darwin
Into the Heart of Borneo by Redmond O'Hanlon
